title: Peanut Butter Blossom Cookies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Soft, salty-sweet peanut butter cookies finished with a chocolate kiss while they are still warm—the kind of tray that disappears at a holiday cookie swap.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment; unwrapping the chocolate kisses first makes the final step calm rather than hurried.
Beat the butter, peanut butter, granulated sugar and brown sugar until creamy and light, scraping the bowl once so no dry sugar is hiding at the bottom.
Beat in the egg and vanilla, then fold in flour, baking soda and salt only until a soft dough forms; overmixing makes these cookies less tender.
Roll level tablespoons of dough into smooth balls, place them well apart on the trays and bake until puffed with lightly set edges, about 9 to 11 minutes.
Let the cookies sit on the hot tray for two minutes, then gently press one chocolate kiss into the centre of every cookie so the base softens without melting away.
Cool completely before stacking; the chocolate needs time to set, and a short rest keeps each blossom neat enough for gifting.
tips: Use a room-temperature egg so the dough comes together evenly.
commonMistakes: Pressing the kisses in immediately can make the cookies spread too much.
substitutions: Use milk chocolate stars in place of kisses if preferred.
storage: Keep airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Balls
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Creamy peanut butter centres dipped in dark chocolate for an easy, crowd-pleasing holiday treat with a little flaky salt on top.
instructions: Line a small tray with parchment and stir the peanut butter, softened butter, powdered sugar and vanilla until the mixture is smooth enough to roll.
Roll the mixture into walnut-size balls and chill them for at least 25 minutes; a firm centre is the easiest way to get a clean chocolate coating.
Melt the chocolate with coconut oil in short microwave bursts, stirring between each burst until glossy; do not let steam or water touch the bowl.
Lower one chilled ball into the chocolate with a fork, lift it out and tap the fork against the bowl so excess chocolate falls back rather than pooling underneath.
Return each coated ball to the tray, add a tiny pinch of flaky salt if using, and chill until the shell is firm and snappy.
Serve slightly cool or pack between parchment layers; the centres taste especially creamy after five minutes at room temperature.
tips: Chill the rolled centres before dipping.
commonMistakes: Overheating chocolate makes the coating thick and grainy.
substitutions: Use semisweet chocolate for a sweeter shell.
storage: Refrigerate airtight for up to 1 week.

title: Christmas Spritz Cookies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Buttery pressed cookies with crisp edges and a tender middle, made for festive shapes, sprinkles and a generous holiday cookie tin.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and leave your baking sheets ungreased; the dough needs a bare surface to release cleanly from a cookie press.
Cream butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the egg, vanilla and almond extract until the bowl smells sweet and nutty.
Mix in flour and salt just until no dry streaks remain; the dough should be soft enough to press but not greasy or sticky.
Load the press, hold it flat against the tray and make one decisive click for each cookie, lifting straight up so the shape stays tidy.
Decorate with sanding sugar before baking, then bake one tray at a time until the edges are set but still pale, about 7 to 9 minutes.
Cool on the tray for five minutes before moving the delicate cookies to a rack, then store only after they are completely cold.
tips: Use room-temperature butter, not melted butter.
commonMistakes: Greasing the tray prevents the dough from releasing from the press.
substitutions: Use lemon extract instead of almond for a brighter cookie.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 5 days.

title: Homemade Eggnog
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A silky, gently spiced homemade eggnog made with a cooked custard base, finished with cream and plenty of fresh nutmeg.
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl until the mixture turns pale and thick enough to leave a ribbon for a second.
Warm milk, cream, cinnamon and nutmeg in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling, then remove the cinnamon stick before tempering the yolks.
Slowly whisk a ladle of warm milk into the yolks, then repeat once more; this gradual step keeps the custard smooth instead of scrambling the eggs.
Pour the tempered mixture back into the pan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it lightly coats a spoon and reaches 160°F.
Strain into a jug, stir in vanilla, and cool to room temperature before chilling for at least two hours so the spices settle into the custard.
Serve cold with freshly grated nutmeg; for the creamiest texture, stir the chilled eggnog well just before pouring.
tips: Use an instant-read thermometer for the cooked custard.
commonMistakes: Boiling the custard can cause it to split.
substitutions: Use half-and-half in place of the milk and cream.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days.
